## Annotation

A remark pinned to a location in something else: `anchor`, `text`, `kind` (`note` / `concern` / `question`), `author`, `createdAt`.

```ts
import { AnnotationField } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/annotation-field';
@field annotations = containsMany(AnnotationField);
```

**`anchor` is a plain string on purpose.** One field then serves every surface a reader can point at: a PDF page (`p.2 ¶3`), a card field path (`severity.level`), a spreadsheet cell, a source line. Typing it per surface would fork the field per consumer.

The `kind` is what makes annotations scannable. A concern raised in the margin of evidence is a finding in waiting; a note is context. Same shape, and the reader must tell them apart without reading every one.

## Example
The contained example is a `concern` anchored at `p.2 ¶3`: a margin remark on a piece of evidence, the kind that becomes a finding when it holds up.

## Non-goals
Not a finding: an annotation is a remark, a Finding is a recorded gap with a severity and a resolution. Not a comment thread — no replies, no participants (Thread owns that shape). Does not resolve or close.

containedExamples.text: The export's timestamps are UTC; the control window is local time, so the 2026-08-20 row may fall outside the period.
